name: Dimmer Switch
description: An in-wall dimmer switch that controls its light locally and can be controlled remotely by Insteon keypads, remotes, sensors, or the Hub. It is rated for up to 150 W of LED or 600 W of incandescent lighting.

steps.text: Turn off power to the switch at the electrical service panel.
Remove the old switch and disconnect the wires. If the box lacks neutral wires, stop and contact support.
Turn on power at the circuit breaker.
Use a voltage detector or multimeter to identify line and load. Line will be energized.
Turn off power at the circuit breaker.
Connect the switch's line, load, neutral and ground wires to the identified wires in the junction box. Make sure the wire nuts are secure and no copper is exposed except the bare ground wire.
Mount the switch into the junction box with the LED bar on the left.
Turn power on to the switch at the circuit breaker panel.
Test the switch by tapping the paddle to turn it on and off. Press and hold to dim or brighten.
Reattach the wall plate.

notes: In three-way and four-way circuits one switch controls the load and the others are secondaries; the diagrams leave the traveler unused at the load switch.

steps.text: Press and hold the SET button until the switch beeps.

notes: Linking is directional: the first device put into linking mode becomes the controller and the second the responder. The switch leaves linking mode on its own once a link is made.

To make the switch a responder, put the controller in linking mode, set the switch to the state the link should recall (on, off or a brightness level), then press and hold its SET button until it double-beeps.
To have two switches control each other, cross-link them: link once in each direction.

verification.note: When adding the switch to the Hub, the Dimmer Switch 2477D Owner's Manual says to hold the SET button until the device beeps, while the Dimmer Switch 2477D Quick Start Guide says until you hear a double-beep. The catalog uses the owner's manual's single beep.

steps.text: Have the Hub start ALL-Linking as the controller, for group 0.
Press and hold the SET button until the switch beeps.
Wait for the Hub to report the new link.
steps.expect: The Hub reports ALL-Linking Completed with the device's Insteon ID

steps.text: Have the Hub send ID Request.
steps.expect: The device answers with its category, subcategory and firmware version

steps.text: Have the Hub send Enter Linking Mode (cmd1 0x09) with cmd2 0x01, for group 1: as an extended message if Get Insteon Engine Version (cmd1 0x0D) says the device is i2CS, and as a standard message otherwise.
Have the Hub start ALL-Linking as the responder.
steps.expect: The Hub reports ALL-Linking Completed with the device's Insteon ID

steps.text: Have the Hub send Ping to confirm the link.

notes: This links the Hub's group 0 to the device as a responder, and the device's group 1 to the Hub as a controller, so the Hub receives the device's reports.

To add the device without its SET button, have the Hub send it Enter Linking Mode (cmd1 0x09, cmd2 0x01; extended for an i2CS device) right after it starts ALL-Linking, in place of the SET button step.

verification.note: Assembled from this profile's linking steps and the standard Insteon commands Start ALL-Linking, ID Request, Enter Linking Mode and Ping; no document describes adding this product to a Hub.

steps.text: Press and hold the SET button until the switch beeps.
Tap the SET button.
Set each device in the scene to the state it should take: on, off or a brightness level.
One at a time, press and hold the SET button on each device in the scene until it double-beeps.
Tap the SET button on the switch to finish building the scene.

notes: The switch stays in multi-linking mode for 4 minutes or until its SET button is tapped.

steps.text: Press and hold the SET button until the switch beeps.
Press and hold the SET button again until the switch beeps.
Press and hold the SET button on the controlled device until it double-beeps; on a multi-button device, tap the button first.

notes: The switch leaves unlinking mode on its own once a link is removed.

To remove several links (multi-unlinking): press and hold the SET button until the switch beeps, press and hold it again, then tap it; hold the SET button on each device until it double-beeps; tap the switch's SET button to exit. The switch stays in this mode for 4 minutes or until its SET button is tapped.

steps.text: Pull the SET button out from the switch until the status LEDs turn off.
Wait about ten seconds.
Push in and hold the SET button until the long beep stops.
Release the SET button.

notes: On older switches that don't give a long beep, press and hold the SET button for 10 seconds.

steps.text: Remove the device from every scene, as a controller and as a responder.

verification.note: Read from how Insteon links work: a device left in a scene keeps links to it in other devices' ALL-Link databases. No document describes removing this product.

steps.text: Remove the device from its scenes first, so no other device keeps links to it.
Have the Hub send Enter Unlinking Mode (cmd1 0x0A) with cmd2 0x01, for group 1, as an extended message if the device is i2CS.
Have the Hub start ALL-Linking as the responder, for group 0.
steps.expect: The device deletes its group 1 link to the Hub

steps.text: Have the Hub start unlinking for group 0 (Start ALL-Linking with link code 0xFF).
Have the Hub send Enter Linking Mode (cmd1 0x09) with cmd2 0x01, for group 1, as an extended message if the device is i2CS.
Wait for the Hub to report that the link is gone.
steps.expect: The Hub reports the device's Insteon ID

verification.note: Assembled from the standard Insteon commands Enter Unlinking Mode, Start ALL-Linking and Enter Linking Mode; no document describes removing this product from a Hub.

notes: The 2015 owner's manual for the 2477S, 2477D and 2477DH prints subcategory 0x00, a template value; Insteon Device Categories (January 2014) gives the 2477D 0x01/0x20.
